title: Wire-format negotiation and client rollback protocol (API standards)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This page defines the standard for wire-format negotiation between Redwood API clients and servers and prescribes a safe client rollback protocol when a contract change results in functional or quality regressions. It is intended for API teams, SDK authors, platform engineers, and SREs who operate change rollouts at the protocol or payload level.

Motivation

- We deploy frequent schema and wire-format changes (streaming, structured outputs, typed events).
- Incompatible or partially compatible changes can cause silent client failures or degraded output quality.
- We need a predictable negotiation handshake, graceful server fallback behavior, and an operational rollback protocol to minimize customer impact.

Goals

1) Define a minimal, backwards-compatible negotiation header set for all Redwood public and internal APIs.
2) Standardize server fallback semantics when a requested wire-version is not supported.
3) Provide a documented client rollback procedure and SDK behaviors that limit blast radius.
4) Specify telemetry and alerting coverage to detect contract regressions within SLA windows.

Non-goals

- Not a schema design guide (use model-serving-standards for structured response contracts).
- Not a replacement for ADRs that authorize breaking changes.

Handshake and negotiation protocol (summary)

1. Client announces: X-Redwood-Wire-Version + X-Redwood-Capabilities header (comma-separated capability tokens).
2. Server responds with: 200 +/- payload and X-Redwood-Wire-Ack header to indicate selected wire version and capability map.
3. If the server cannot honor the requested wire version, it returns a structured fallback response with X-Redwood-Wire-Ack and an explanatory X-Redwood-Wire-Reason.

Required headers and semantics

- X-Redwood-Wire-Version: integer (client-preferred, e.g., 7). Means the highest wire revision the client understands.
- X-Redwood-Capabilities: short tokens (examples: streaming_v2, partial_checkpoint, typed_events). Negotiated on a best-effort basis.
- X-Redwood-Wire-Ack: server-picked integer indicating the wire version used for the response. If absent, client must treat response as using legacy wire semantics (version 0).
- X-Redwood-Wire-Reason: optional short string when a downgrade or fallback is applied (e.g., "downgrade-unsupported-capability").
- X-Redwood-Wire-Experimental: optional boolean token when server advertises unstable extensions. Clients MUST NOT auto-enable experimental features without opt-in.

Server behavior and fallback modes

- Mode: Strict (default for private & dedicated tiers): if client requests unsupported wire version or critical capability, respond 400 with structured error and suggested fallback version in X-Redwood-Wire-Ack.
- Mode: Lenient (default for hosted public API during staged rollouts): server may automatically downgrade to a compatible lower wire version while attaching X-Redwood-Wire-Reason and a compatibility warning in the response body.
- Mode: Quarantine (used during incident response): server returns HTTP 503 with Retry-After and a single-line reason token. Quarantine is only used by operator action or an automated rollout gate failure.

Client SDK responsibilities

- Always send X-Redwood-Wire-Version and X-Redwood-Capabilities on every request.
- Observe X-Redwood-Wire-Ack: if ack < requested and ack < client's minimum_supported_version, surface a clear error and (by default) disable the affected feature path.
- Backoff and retry policy: on 400 with fallback suggestion, attempt one in-process downgrade if the downgrade is read-only and does not change semantics. Avoid automatic downgrades that change output shapes.
- Opt-in for experimental features: expose an SDK flag (e.g., enable_experimentals) that must be explicit and logged.
- Telemetry: increment counters for (wire_request_version, wire_ack_version, capability_mismatch, downgrade_applied).

Rollout, migration and testing checklist (for API changes)

1) Author ADR: document the intended wire revisions, compatibility classification (non-breaking|additive|breaking), and migration timeline.
2) Automated contract tests: add unit and integration tests that assert behavior across X-Redwood-Wire-Version permutations.
3) SDK canary: publish SDK build that nominates the new wire_version and tests against a mirrored staging endpoint.
4) Beta flagging: expose capability tokens behind an opt-in beta flag for 7 days with synthetic and real-customer telemetry.
5) Gradual ramp: 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with canary validations at each step (see telemetry gating rules).

Telemetry gating and alerting (minimum set)

- Metrics (all counters and histograms must include wire_ack_version as a dimension):
  - wire.requests_total (tags: client_version, wire_request_version)
  - wire.acks_total (tags: wire_ack_version, capability_mismatch)
  - wire.downgrades_applied_total
  - wire.errors_by_kind (bad-schema, missing-field, type-mismatch)
  - client.rollback_actions_total
- Alerts (examples):
  - Alert A1: spike in wire.errors_by_kind[type-mismatch] > 0.5% of requests over 10m -> P1 runbook trigger.
  - Alert A2: downgrades_applied_total rate > baseline*5 for 15m -> Investigate release.
  - Alert A3: client.rollback_actions_total > 0 from multiple distinct customers -> Customer outreach and pause rollout.

Compatibility test matrix (table)

| Client min | Client prefer | Server ack | Expected behavior | Action on mismatch |
|------------|---------------|------------|-------------------|--------------------|
| 0          | 0             | 0          | Legacy semantics  | none               |
| 1          | 2             | 1          | Downgraded        | SDK logs warning    |
| 2          | 4             | 3          | Partial features  | feature-disabled    |
| 3          | 3             | 3          | Compatible        | proceed             |

Operational rollback protocol (step-by-step)

1) Detection: automated alert or customer report indicating repeated type/schema mismatches or defined error budget breach.
2) Activate cooldown: set deployment traffic to Lenient -> Quarantine mode for the affected model/service.
3) Notify: page oncall, post incident stub to #ops-release.
4) Execute rollback: either server-side rollback to previous artifact or set X-Redwood-Wire-Ack override policy to pin to previous version.
5) Monitor: watch wire.errors_by_kind and client.rollback_actions_total for 30m.
6) Postmortem: publish a short RCA within 48 hours and an ADR for any deemed-required long-term change.

Runbook snippets (commands and samples)

- Force server to respond with chosen wire ack (operator API):
  curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/rollout/override \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"service":"nlp-serve-prod","wire_ack_override":2,"reason":"rollback-due-to-schema-failure"}'

- Client header example (curl):
  curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $USER_TOKEN' \n    -H 'X-Redwood-Wire-Version: 4' \n    -H 'X-Redwood-Capabilities: streaming_v2,typed_events' \n    -d '{"prompt":"Translate to French"}'

Observability consoles and dashboards

- Create a "Wire Version Health" dashboard with the following panels:
  - Time series: wire.requests_total by wire_request_version and wire_ack_version.
  - Heatmap: errors_by_kind split by customer and wire_ack_version.
  - Single statistic: percentage of downgraded responses in the last 30m.
  - Top 10 customers by client.rollback_actions_total.

SLO / performance considerations

- Wire negotiation should add no more than 2ms median overhead; include that in the service's latency budget.
- When Lenient downgrade is applied, log the additional latency and track as a feature degradation dimension.

Security and privacy notes

- Wire headers must not contain PII. Capability tokens are short, non-sensitive identifiers.
- Experimental capabilities MUST NOT enable data exfiltration or unencrypted telemetry.

Ownership and cadence

- Primary owner: API Platform team (engineering).
- Review cadence: quarterly or on every major protocol ADR.
- Change process: breaking changes require ADR approval and opt-in SDK release prior to server-side enforcement.

Appendix: example JSON negotiation response (text)

{
  "status":"ok",
  "wire_ack":3,
  "warnings":["downgrade-unsupported-capability"],
  "payload_schema":"v3/structured-output"
}

References

- See the ADRs for protocol adaptor and validation contract for detailed decision history.
- SDK implementation reference: internal sdk-client/wire-negotiation module.
